chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. 'Imran al-Ash'ari from Muhammad b. 'Ali from 'Isa b. 'Abdullah al-'Alawi al-'Amri from his father from his forefathers from 'Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:
O Allah, have mercy on my vicegerents — three times. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who are your vicegerents? He said: Those who convey my narrations and my Sunna, then teach them to my Nation.

key_terms.حَدِيثِي وَسُنَّتِي: my narrations and my Sunna -- the two pillars of prophetic legacy
key_terms.خُلَفَائِي: my vicegerents / my successors -- not political rulers but those who carry forward the Prophet's knowledge
key_terms.يُبَلِّغُونَ: convey / transmit -- emphasizing the act of faithful transmission
key_terms.يُعَلِّمُونَهَا أُمَّتِي: teach them to my Nation -- the second duty of successors: pedagogy

ai.seo_question: Who are the vicegerents (khulafa) of the Prophet Muhammad according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this well-known prophetic tradition narrated through Imam 'Ali (AS), the Prophet Muhammad (S) invokes divine mercy upon his 'vicegerents' (khulafa'), repeating the supplication three times for emphasis. When asked to identify these vicegerents, the Prophet defines them not as political successors but as scholars and transmitters who preserve his teachings — those who convey his hadiths and his Sunna, and then teach them to the Muslim community. This hadith has been widely cited by Shia scholars to establish the authority and merit of hadith transmitters and religious scholars as the true successors of the Prophet.
